Subject: Re: Saturday alarm

Hi Kristen,

Here’s my account of what happened Saturday. At about 10:40, I put a bag of butter popcorn in the break room microwave, hit the popcorn button, and went back out front. A customer needed a shear pin for his snowblower, and helping him took longer than I expected—maybe six or seven minutes. By the time I got back, the popcorn had burned and set off the alarm.

The store was cleared for about 25 minutes. Thankfully, nobody was hurt and there was no damage—just smoke and the smell of burnt popcorn. The crew from Engine [number, if you know it] came out. One of them was Mikey Szymanski, who I broke in as a probie back in ’03. I’m sure I’ll hear about this from him for a while.

For the record, September’s alarm wasn’t mine; that was the sensor in the paint aisle. But this one is on me, not the microwave. After 31 years on the job, my first alarm as a civilian was over a bag of butter popcorn. Even my wife said the van smelled like a burnt movie theater.

I’m sorry for putting the customers and the store through that, especially the Hendersons. I hope they’ll be back, but I feel bad that they left their cart behind. I understand the $175 dispatch bill, and I’m happy to cover it. You can take it from my check, or I can bring cash—your call. I’ll also buy Denise the coffee I owe her.

I like working Saturdays with the weekend crowd, and I need the hours for heating oil. I hope I can keep my shifts. I know I need to be more careful, and I won’t use the break room microwave for popcorn again.

Walt
